I give up.

The statement is Putnam 2015 A6, and I don't have a proof I can formalize within these constraints. The argument I see is the following. Since AM = MB, A preserves im M and B preserves ker M. Comparing charpolys on those invariant subspaces gives equal charpolys for the induced quotient maps. Then det(A − MX) = det[[A, M],[X, I]] = det[[B, X],[M, I]] = det(B − XM) via Schur complements. Making this work in Lean needs basis changes to block-triangular form, charpoly multiplicativity over invariant subspaces, and the block-determinant identities. I did not get that to compile, and I did not check the Mathlib lemma names. The file `/work/putnam_2015_a6.lean` is unchanged and still contains the `sorry`.
